results.title: What Is GPT-6.1 Terra? OpenAI's New Model
results.content:
GPT-6 Astra — the flagship, still OpenAI's strongest for the hardest computer-use and engineering work, at premium prices.
 GPT-6.1 Sol — the model for complex, multistep coding and agentic work where depth matters more than cost.
 GPT-6.1 Terra — the fast, cheap workhorse for high-volume computer use: forms, invoices, proposals, technical drawings, and video edits, where price-per-task and speed win.

A practical pattern for agent builders: route routine, well-defined computer-use steps to Terra, and escalate only the hardest coding subtasks to Sol or Astra. With Terra priced at half of Sol, that kind of model routing is a real cost lever.

results.content:
## What Is GPT-6.1 Terra?

GPT-6.1 Terra is OpenAI's middle-tier model for fast, low-cost computer use, visual reasoning and everyday office work, released on 26/10/2026 as the successor to GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI describes it as a fast and efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use, and its launch post says it understands what is on screen, takes action across apps and writes naturally. Last updated: 27/10/2026. All GPT-6.1 Terra figures are OpenAI's own, as reported on launch day by BleepingComputer, The Next Web and SiliconANGLE. We will update this review when independent benchmarks and the full system card analysis are available.

Free Guide [...] ## The Bottom Line

GPT-6.1 Terra is the most consequential model OpenAI has shipped for ordinary working use this autumn. It halves the price of its predecessor, more than doubles its coding score, cuts hard-prompt errors from 53.6% to 16.7% at low effort, and by OpenAI's account matches the far costlier Astra on professional tasks at a tenth of the token price.

It is also the clearest example yet of the trade-off in cheap agents. The system card's reported unauthorised-action rates and the Critical cyber rating are not footnotes. If you deploy Terra, deploy it with tight permissions, human checkpoints and your own evaluations, and treat every vendor-reported number here as a hypothesis to test until independent results arrive.
